### Resolved 2026-10-21 — MCP wire input is tolerant where MCP is

Extends "Schemas and serde describe the wire form" above, which said nothing about input tolerance. `CallToolResult` deserialization required `isError` and `structuredContent`, and `ContentBlock` required `annotations.audience`, so valid MCP results from other servers failed to parse.

- **Input:** only `content` is required. `isError` defaults to `false`, an absent or `null` `structuredContent` becomes the empty string, `annotations` and `annotations.audience` default to no audience, and other annotation fields are ignored. A non-object `structuredContent` and a non-`"text"` content block are still rejected.
- **Output:** `structuredContent` is omitted when empty, never `null`. Serializing a `CallToolResult` whose `structured_content` is not empty and not a JSON object is a serde error, because MCP requires an object; `CallToolResult::try_new` checks the same thing up front.
- **Retry-After:** `parse_retry_after` accepts all three HTTP-date forms RFC 9110 §5.6.7 requires (IMF-fixdate, RFC 850, asctime), not just IMF-fixdate; see "`parse_retry_after()` format details".

### Resolved 2026-10-21 — Schemas only for types serde serializes
- **One layer per export.** Each `*_js(Unknown…)` export used to call a public "Rust-typed core" (`render_toon(JsToonOptions)`, `JsAgentResponse::items` and a dozen more) that repeated the length checks by hand: 14 `> MAX_HINTS`-style checks next to `input::check_len`. Nothing outside the module called the cores. The exports now convert through `input`, which owns every limit, and call a private function; `michi_core::napi` exposes only `num`. `napi.rs` (3,037 lines) is split by concern into `napi/{toon,hints,outcome,resilience,response,value}.rs` beside `input.rs` and `num.rs`. The JS API and `index.d.ts` types are unchanged (the generated file was diffed before and after; only doc comments differ). `ToonOptions.rows` and `StatusItem.value` carry an explicit `ts_type`, because napi-derive resolves a field's type name only for modules it has already expanded.
- **One conversion for a cell.** `js_value_to_rust` and `js_kv_value_to_rust` were copies of one validation. `JsToonValue::into_cell` checks the `type` tag and its payload once; TOON tables and KV lines convert from that.
- **Label parsing lives in core.** `ErrorCode::ALL` with `FromStr`, and `StepStatus::ALL` with `from_labels` (and `StepLabelError`), are the inverse of `label()` and `reason()`, built from the same tables. The NAPI copies (a string `match` per enum and three hand-written "expected one of" lists) are gone, and tests check the `ts_args_type` unions against `ALL`. A unit test names every variant without a wildcard, so a new one fails to compile until it is listed.
- **The byte budget bounds the output (16 MiB, was 64 MiB).** The 64 MiB budget limited input only. A control character renders to 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON and 19 in `toCallToolResult()`, so 64 MiB of input could produce 1.2 GiB, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. Measured in Node before the change (60 one-MiB control-character values): `renderText()` 377 MB, 1.2 GiB RSS, 2.4 s; `renderJson()` rendered, then threw `GenericFailure`, 1.6 GiB RSS; `toCallToolResult()` 25 s, 3.2 GiB. At 16 MiB the worst render is 19 x 16 MiB = 304 MiB, under V8's limit, so a response renders or is rejected by the budget before any rendering. A `const` assertion ties the cap to the string limit, and a unit test pins the factor 19 for every ASCII byte. Considered: charging each control character at its escaped size (exact, but it adds a second accounting table that must follow every escape rule, and plain ASCII gains nothing), and an estimate-then-render check in each render (the budget already is that estimate).
- **Compatibility:** inputs over 16 MiB of strings per call, or per `AgentResponse`, are now rejected where up to 64 MiB was accepted. Pre-1.0, and no known consumer sends that much; the error names the cap.
---
michi-core: minor
michi-node: minor
---

michi-core: what a response reports about itself now has one source each, so its text and JSON cannot contradict each other. A section's `truncated` is derived (its total is above its count), the budget's `sections[n]` roll-up is written from the response's own sections, and the budget's `truncated` is also true whenever a section was cut. The root keys michi writes itself are one reserved list for every writer, and it now includes the error document's keys, so a successful response can no longer render an `error:` / `message:` document from caller data. A provenance label `fingerprint` is always rejected, because it read exactly like the real fingerprint.

Breaking: `Section`'s fields are private; read them with `name()`, `body()`, `count()`, `total()` and `truncated()`. `Section::truncated(bool)` and `Section::returned_count(n)` are removed; a text section that stands for several items is `Section::text_with_count(name, body, n)`, and `SectionBody::Text` is now `Text { text, count }`. `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section()` are removed, and the budget's JSON no longer has a `sections` array (the response's `sections` carries those counts). `truncated_section` now takes `(name, fields, &outcome, row, guidance)` and builds the rows from `outcome.kept`. `budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `truncated`, `error`, `message`, `causes` and `exit_code` join `totalCount`, `help` and `recovery` as reserved: as a type name (`render_toon`, `list`, `empty_state`), a KV key (`render_kv`, `kv_items`) or a section name they are a validation error, and the error messages list the reserved keys.

Migration: `.truncated_section(Section::toon(name, f, rows), &outcome, g)` becomes `.truncated_section(name, f, &outcome, |item| row_of(item), g)`. Drop `.truncated(..)` on sections and `.section(SectionCost::new(..))` on budgets. Rename any KV key or list named after a reserved key (for example a `message` field becomes `commit_message`). In JavaScript, `renderKv`, `renderToon`, `emptyState` and `kvItems` reject the same reserved names.

import sys

root = sys.argv[1]
p = root + '/docs/spec/06-decisions.md'
s = open(p).read()


def must(old, new):
    global s
    if old not in s:
        raise SystemExit(f"missing {old[:90]!r}")
    s = s.replace(old, new, 1)


must('''### `error::DomainError` and `error::Error` are two types, not one
''', '''### `error::DomainError` and `error::Error` are two types, not one

> Superseded 2026-11-16: `Error` and the `Result` alias are removed, and `class()` and `is_retryable()` moved onto
> `DomainError`. See "Invariants live behind private fields; `Error` is gone" below.
''')
must('''- **Output:** `structuredContent` is omitted when empty, never `null`. Serializing a `CallToolResult` whose `structured_content` is not empty and not a JSON object is a serde error, because MCP requires an object; `CallToolResult::try_new` checks the same thing up front.''',
     '''- **Output:** `structuredContent` is omitted when empty, never `null`. Serializing a `CallToolResult` whose `structured_content` is not empty and not a JSON object is a serde error, because MCP requires an object; `CallToolResult::try_new` checks the same thing up front. (Superseded 2026-11-16: `structured_content` is an `Option<JsonObject>`, checked when built, so no result fails to serialize and `try_new` is gone.)''')
must('''Their fields stay public (readable and assignable); struct literals''',
     '''Their fields stay public (readable and assignable; amended 2026-11-16 for types with an invariant, see "Invariants live behind private fields"); struct literals''')

s = s.rstrip('\n') + '''

### Resolved 2026-11-16 — Invariants live behind private fields; `Error` is gone

Reverses "Public types can grow" (2026-10-21) where it kept every field "readable and assignable": that decision weighed
ergonomics and additive growth, not types whose fields carry a rule the constructor enforces. The architecture audit of
0.10.0 broke three such rules through plain field writes, each reproduced as a failing test before the change
(`tests/api_invariants.rs`):

- `RetryConfig::try_new` rejects a zero `max_delay` because zero drops a server's `Retry-After`. Setting
  `cfg.max_delay = Duration::ZERO` afterwards made `next_retry_delay(&cfg, 0, 0.5, Some(60 s))` return 0 ns, a hot
  retry against a server that asked for a minute. `michi-pipeline` re-exports `RetryConfig`.
- `DomainError`'s builder keeps `MAY_HAVE_TAKEN_EFFECT_HINT` present exactly while a `Timeout` is not retryable.
  `e.retryable = true` on a timeout kept the hint, so the JSON said `retryable: true` and the help said not to retry
  blindly; `e.code = Timeout` on a `RateLimited` error gave a retryable timeout with no hint, the unsafe retry the hint
  exists for. `michi-pipeline`'s own `AmbiguousOutcome` conversion wrote `retryable = false` directly and so skipped the
  hint; with the builder a timeout source now carries core's verify-first hint, and the pipeline adds its own
  `VERIFY_BEFORE_RETRY_HINT` only when core's is absent, so the agent reads one, not two.
- `PartialSuccess` took the same operation index in `completed`, `failed` and `skipped` (op 0 rendered completed and
  failed, `exit=1`), and a completed operation's `reason` was accepted and silently not rendered.

At 1.0 a public field freezes the layout and makes such a rule unenforceable for good. `michi-pipeline` and
`michi-graph` already keep their fields private behind getters, so core now follows them where it matters.

- **Private, with getters:** `DomainError` (`code()`, `message()`, `causes()`, `hints()`, `get_recovery()`,
  `get_retry_after()`, `is_retryable()`), `RetryConfig` (`max_retries()`, `base_delay()`, `max_delay()`,
  `jitter_factor()`) and `PartialSuccess` (`completed()`, `failed()`, `skipped()`, built with `try_new`, which returns
  `DuplicateOpIndex`). `Section` went private the same day ("Envelope facts have one source"). The compiler is the
  proof: `compile_fail,E0616` doctests on each type assert the error code for the audit's field writes.
- **Still public:** plain records with no rule across fields: `KvItem`, `ProvenanceEntry`, `FailedOp`, `RecoveryHint`,
  `StatusItem`, `StatusResponse`, `PipelineStep`, `Pipeline`, `ContentBlock`, `CallToolResult`, and the newtypes.
- **States the domain forbids:** `OpRef` is split into `CompletedOp` (no reason, so none can be dropped) and
  `SkippedOp`; the JS `renderPartialSuccess` takes the same two shapes, rejects a non-null `reason` on a completed op and
  throws on a repeated index. `Pipeline.id` is removed: nothing rendered it, `renderPipeline` passed an empty string,
  and `RunRecord::to_pipeline` filled it for no reader. Rejected: rendering it (`pipeline: <id>`), which would change a
  document no consumer asked to change; `RunRecord::run_id()` already gives the id.
- **`CallToolResult.structured_content` is `Option<JsonObject>`.** It was a `String` where empty meant none, checked
  only by `try_new` or at serialization, both behind `serde`, so a default-feature caller could build a result that
  could not serialize. `JsonObject::new` checks the text in every build with a strict RFC 8259 checker in `mcp.rs` that
  applies `serde_json`'s limits (127 levels, no lone surrogate escapes, finite numbers); a property test compares the
  two. michi's own renderers wrap their writers' output directly. The field stays public: the type now carries the
  rule. The wire shape is unchanged.
- **`michi_core::Error` and `Result` are removed.** No michi API returned them (every fallible function has its own
  error type; `michi-pipeline` converts to `DomainError`), monokl builds `DomainError` directly, and
  `Error::InvalidInput`/`NotFound` duplicated `ErrorCode` minus hints, recovery and causes. ADR 9 says such surface goes
  before 1.0. `class()` and `is_retryable()` live on `DomainError`; `is_retryable()` is `true` exactly when `class()` is
  `Transient`.
- **One convention for builders and getters** (spec 03, "API conventions"): builders are bare and consuming (`x(v)` sets
  or appends one, `xs(vec)` replaces a list); getters are bare, `is_x()` for a `bool`, and `get_x()` only when a builder
  of the same type holds the bare name, as `std::process::Command::get_args` does. Considered: `with_x` builders (would
  rename every builder in core and `michi-pipeline` to free a few getter names) and getters named after their type
  (`recovery_hint()` would read as `AgentResponse`'s appending builder of the same name). Applied:
  `StatusResponse::with_hints` became `hints`; `render_already_done` takes `&[Hint]` like every other renderer;
  `DomainError::render()` and `render_json()` became `render(OutputFormat)`, like `AgentResponse`; text-only types keep
  `render()`. `DomainError::context(prefix)` replaces the field write `e.message = format!(…)` the docs used to
  suggest, and `retry_after(None)` clears a delay.
- **Derives that were missing:** `Hash` on `ErrorCode` and `ErrorClass`, `Display` on `ErrorCode` (its label),
  `PartialEq` on `DomainError`, `Eq` on `AttemptRecord`, and `FromStr` plus `Borrow<str>` on `StepId` and `RunId`, so
  `"x".parse::<StepId>()` works and a `BTreeMap<StepId, _>` is looked up with a `&str`. `Hint`'s `Eq`/`Hash` belong to
  the hints module's owner and are not part of this change.
'''
open(p, 'w').write(s)

1:# Pipeline execution (`michi-pipeline`)
5:This document describes the API that replaced `execute_pipeline`, `execute_pipeline_parallel` and `StepDependencies` (see [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md), "Pipeline execution redesign"). The design follows the research report in [`docs/research/pipeline-design.md`](../research/pipeline-design.md).
11:- `RunId` names one run. It has the same charset. The caller supplies it, because only the caller knows what a run is (one agent request, one job). `RunId::unique(prefix)` builds `{prefix}-{millis}-{pid}-{counter}-{random}` (numbers in base 36, each after its own `-`, so two processes cannot print the same digits) without a UUID dependency. `random` is 64 bits from `std::collections::hash_map::RandomState`, whose keys are random per process, hashed with the time, pid and counter. Without it, containers started in the same millisecond all had pid 1 and counter 0 and so the same id, and the run id is the prefix of the idempotency key: a collision makes a deduplicating downstream treat new work as a repeat of old work. The result is unique with overwhelming probability, not by construction; a caller who needs a global guarantee should supply its own UUID through `RunId::try_new`. The random part takes 14 of the 64 bytes, so keep the prefix to about 30 bytes.
50:`StepContext` carries the run id, step id, attempt number (0-based), a cancellation token that is a child of the run's token, the step's deadline if one is set (the earlier of its own and its group's), when the executor will cut this attempt (`attempt_deadline()`) and the attempt timeout configured for the step (`attempt_timeout()`). `idempotency_key()` is `run_id:step_id`. It stays the same across attempts and across resume, so a step that passes it to a deduplicating downstream gets each effect applied once. The attempt number is for logging and backoff only and is never part of the key.
226:`Pipeline::render()` emits `step[N]{id,name,status,reason}:` with snake_case labels (`completed_earlier`, `outcome_unknown`, `not_run`, ...) and a reason (`prerequisite_failed`, `cancelled`, `circuit_open`, `unverified`, `start_not_recorded`, `timeout`, `gateway`, `interrupted`, `step_failed`) or `null`. It stays TOON 4.4 conformant.
239:- `to_pipeline()` and `render()`: the michi-core `Pipeline` view and its TOON.
323:Retries are jittered. Without `ExecOptions::jitter_seed`, each retry's jitter seed is derived from the run id, step id and attempt number (FNV-1a with a splitmix64 finalizer, mapped to `[0, 1)`), so steps that fail together back off by different amounts instead of retrying in lockstep, while the same run and plan always wait the same delays. `jitter_seed(x)` fixes one seed for every retry of every step, as before.

input.content:
refactor(core)!: keep invariants behind private fields before 1.0

Public fields let callers skip the checks the constructors make: a zero
max_delay after RetryConfig::try_new gave a 0 ns retry against
Retry-After: 60s, and writing DomainError.retryable or .code left a
retryable timeout without its verify-first hint. michi-pipeline's own
AmbiguousOutcome conversion did the same field write and lost the hint.

DomainError, RetryConfig and PartialSuccess now keep their fields
private behind getters, and compile_fail,E0616 doctests prove the
audit's writes no longer compile. This reverses the 2026-10-21 "fields
stay public" decision for types with a cross-field rule; 06-decisions
records why. Plain records stay public.

States the domain forbids are now unrepresentable: PartialSuccess is
built with try_new and rejects a repeated index, completed ops carry no
reason (OpRef splits into CompletedOp and SkippedOp), and the dead
Pipeline.id is gone. CallToolResult.structured_content is an
Option<JsonObject> checked in every build, so every result serializes;
the wire shape is unchanged.

michi_core::Error and Result had no producer and are removed; class()
and is_retryable() move onto DomainError. Builders and getters follow
one written convention (spec 03), DomainError renders through
render(OutputFormat), and small types gain the derives they lacked.

W2-B, API invariants before 1.0. Based on `integration/hardening`.

## What and why

Types whose fields carry a rule now keep those fields private, so the checks their constructors make hold for the life of the value. Each audit example was reproduced as a failing test first:

- `RetryConfig::try_new` then `cfg.max_delay = 0` gave a 0 ns retry against `Retry-After: 60s`.
- `DomainError.retryable = true` on a timeout kept the verify-first hint.
- `DomainError.code = Timeout` on a `RateLimited` error gave a retryable timeout with no hint. michi-pipeline's `AmbiguousOutcome` conversion did the same field write and dropped the hint.

Per audit finding:

- **arch #3 (fixed):** `DomainError`, `RetryConfig` and `PartialSuccess` now have private fields with getters. Plain records stay public. This reverses the 2026-10-21 "fields stay public" decision for these types, and `06-decisions.md` records why.
- **arch #5 (fixed):** `michi_core::Error` and `Result` are deleted. `class()` and `is_retryable()` are now on `DomainError`.
- **arch #10 (fixed):** one written rule for builders and getters, in spec 03 under "API conventions":
  - `StatusResponse::with_hints` is renamed to `hints`.
  - `render_already_done` takes `&[Hint]`.
  - `DomainError::render()` and `render_json()` are replaced by `render(OutputFormat)`.
- **arch #11 (fixed):**
  - `Pipeline.id` is removed.
  - `PartialSuccess::try_new` rejects a repeated index.
  - `OpRef` is split into `CompletedOp` (no reason) and `SkippedOp`.
  - JS `renderPartialSuccess` throws on either case.
- **arch #12 (fixed):** `structured_content` is now `Option<JsonObject>`, checked in every build by a strict RFC 8259 checker. A proptest compares that checker against serde_json. The wire shape is unchanged.
- **rust-perf #8 (fixed for owned types):**
  - `Hash` on `ErrorCode` and `ErrorClass`.
  - `Display` on `ErrorCode`.
  - `PartialEq` on `DomainError`.
  - `Eq` on `AttemptRecord`.
  - `FromStr` and `Borrow<str>` on `StepId` and `RunId`.
  - `Hint` is left to W2-A.

## Decisions

- Getters use the bare field name. When a builder already uses that name, the getter is `get_x()` (`get_recovery`, `get_retry_after`), as in std's `Command::get_args`.
- New `DomainError::context(prefix)`. `retry_after` now takes `impl Into<Option<Duration>>`, so `None` clears it.
- An `AmbiguousOutcome` from a timeout now carries core's verify-first hint. The pipeline adds its own hint only when core's is missing, so the agent gets one hint, not two.

## Edits outside W2-B's files (one-line call-site fixes)

- `response.rs`: `to_call_tool_result`, plus 5 test lines.
- `napi/response.rs`: 1 line.
- `napi/toon.rs`: `with_hints` → `hints`.
- Tests that referenced `Error`, `OpRef` or `render_json`.
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/{error_text,mcp_wire,resilience}.rs`.

| `just clippy` | 0 |

| `just typos` | 0 |
| `just check` (includes doc-check, fuzz-check, deny, zizmor, md fmt) | 0 |
| `cargo test --doc` (core, pipeline) | 0 |
| `pnpm build && pnpm test` in michi-node (184 passed) | 0 |

The `compile_fail,E0616` doctests assert the error code. The trybuild `.stderr` files were regenerated and reviewed.

- each private field made `pub`: all 4 compile_fail doctests fail
- `try_new` accepts duplicates
- `class` ignores `retryable`
- checker without the surrogate check, the depth limit, or the finite-number check
- pipeline adds a second hint
